text:
alex_support: @sara_sales heads-up — NimbusAI (customer) hitting repeated 429s overnight. Error payloads show `quota_exceeded`. They have a demo tomorrow morning and say this started after a key rotation.

nimbus_ops: quick context — we run large nightly ingest jobs. Yesterday we peaked ~1.7M tokens/day, with short bursts of ~400 concurrent requests. Keys were rotated ~18:20 UTC. Sample response and headers below from one failed request.

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
error: quota_exceeded
```

jamie_eng: thanks — two likely vectors: (1) per-key/minute concurrency/cap hit (we have 60 reqs/min default on free), (2) billing hold / plan ceilings. Can you paste account id and confirm whether traffic is split across multiple keys or just one?

nimbus_ops: account: acct-67321. We have 3 API keys, but the ingest process didn't rotate evenly so most traffic went through `key-1` during the spike.

alex_support: noted. I ran a quick account check — account acct-67321 is on Free org plan and there's an outstanding invoice flagged. That will keep them on free caps. I'm opening an internal ticket now to request a temporary concurrency uplift while billing sorts payment.

billing_bot: Billing hold detected for acct-67321 — unpaid invoice INV-2024-253. Auto-upgrade/bridge blocked until payment or manual override. To request override, include invoice receipts and cc billing@redwood.com.

sara_sales: I can coordinate a sales-assisted upgrade. For tomorrow's demo we can either (A) do a 24h temporary uplift on hosted capacity, or (B) switch them to a paid monthly plan with higher concurrency. Which do they prefer?

nimbus_ops: temporary uplift is fine for now — just need the demo to work and then we'll finalize payment for monthly. Please confirm by 09:00 PST.

jamie_eng: engineering mitigation guidance in the meantime:
- spread traffic across keys (rotate evenly)
- reduce per-request parallelism and add client-side batching
- implement exponential backoff with jitter on 429s
Example very small pseudo-snippet for batching/spacing:
```
async def send_batches(items):
  for batch in chunk(items, 16):
    await client.generate(batch)
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)  # slight spacing to avoid hot bursts
```
Also check that token rotation didn't accidentally create duplicate clients hammering the same key.

alex_support: created ticket SUP-9832 to request a 24h +50% concurrency bridge for acct-67321 and flagged it P1 (demo). Added invoice context. Request submitted to billing and eng.

sara_sales: pinged billing and legal for manual override and emailed customer with upgrade options. I'll propose the paid hosted plan (monthly) with 2x baseline concurrency; if they want more we can scope Dedicated.

billing_bot: Manual override requested — reference SUP-9832. Billing will process once payment proof received or after sales approval.

alex_support: temporary uplift applied at 23:12 UTC (SUP-9832) — please monitor and post any new 429s here. If errors persist include new x-request-id values and last_failed_ts.

nimbus_ops: confirming — traffic looks stable now. No 429s for the last 12 minutes. Thank you all. We'll finalize payment today.

jamie_eng: follow-ups for customer: add batching, rotate keys evenly, and set client-side retries with jitter. For long-term heavy ingest recommend reserved capacity (Dedicated) or paid hosted with a higher commit.

alex_support: closing this thread once sara confirms sales uplift processed. Reopen if any new errors. :thumbsup:
